name: A linear interpolator
brief:
A price series has gaps and arrives in any order. Write `interp(xs, ys, x)`. It returns the straight-line value at `x` between the two nearest known points.

A missing `y` is `None` or NaN. Drop it before you interpolate.
definition:
Sort the points by $x$ and average the $y$ values that share an $x$. For $x_0 \le x \le x_1$, the neighbours either side of $x$, return

$$y = y_0 + (y_1 - y_0)\dfrac{x - x_0}{x_1 - x_0}$$

Below the smallest $x$ or above the largest, return the nearest end value. If no point is left, raise `ValueError`.
constraints: Find the bracketing pair with `bisect`, not by scanning every pair. The tests check results and speed, not the method.
hint: Build a dict from $x$ to a list of $y$ values, skipping missing ones. Sort its keys, then use `bisect.bisect_right`.
starter:
def interp(xs, ys, x):

    Repeated x are averaged; the ends hold; no point raises ValueError."""

examples.note: A quarter of the way across, so a quarter of the rise of 100.
The missing value is dropped, then time 1 is a quarter of the way across.

tests.name: Two points
tests.why: A quarter of the way from 100 to 200 is 125.

tests.name: Unsorted input
tests.why: Sort by x before you look for the bracket.

tests.name: Below the smallest x
tests.why: Hold the first value; do not extrapolate.

tests.name: Above the largest x
tests.why: Hold the last value; do not extrapolate.

tests.name: An exact point
tests.why: At a known x the answer is its y.

tests.name: Repeated x, at the repeat
tests.why: The two readings at x = 1 average to 15.

tests.name: Repeated x, between
tests.why: Average the repeats first, then go halfway to 30.

tests.name: A missing y on uneven times
tests.why: Drop the missing y; by position it would be 106.

tests.name: A NaN y
tests.why: A NaN is missing too. One point is left beyond 1, so the end value holds.

tests.name: One point
tests.why: One point is both ends, so its value holds everywhere.

tests.name: A missing y at the left end
tests.why: Drop the missing y. Below the smallest remaining x, hold the first value.

tests.name: Long input, sampled
tests.call: interp(list(range(100000)), [2 * i for i in range(100000)], 54321.5)
tests.why: 100,000 points must still finish well inside the 5-second limit.

tests.name: Every y missing
tests.why: No point is left once the missing y values go, so raise ValueError.

how: Submit runs 14 hidden tests. Each answer is accepted when `math.isclose(actual, expected, rel_tol=1e-9)`.
